evals.prompt: I want to A/B test our homepage headline. We currently say 'The All-in-One Project Management Tool' and want to test something benefit-focused. We get about 15,000 visitors/month and our current signup rate is 3.2%.
evals.expected_output: Should check for product-marketing.md first. Should build a proper hypothesis using the framework: 'Because [observation], we believe [change] will cause [outcome], which we'll measure by [metric].' Should identify this as an A/B test (two variants). Should calculate or reference sample size needs based on 15,000 monthly visitors and 3.2% baseline. Should define primary metric (signup rate), secondary metrics, and guardrail metrics. Should warn about the peeking problem and recommend a fixed test duration. Should provide the test plan in the structured output format.
assertions: Checks for product-marketing.md
Uses the hypothesis framework with observation, belief, outcome, and metric
Identifies as A/B test type
Addresses sample size calculation based on traffic and baseline rate
Defines primary metric (signup rate)
Defines secondary and guardrail metrics
Warns about the peeking problem
Provides structured test plan output

evals.prompt: we want to test like 4 different CTA button colors on our pricing page. is that a good idea?
evals.expected_output: Should trigger on casual phrasing. Should identify this as an A/B/n test (multiple variants). Should caution that testing 4 variants requires significantly more traffic than a simple A/B test. Should reference the sample size quick reference showing traffic multipliers for multiple variants. Should question whether button color alone is likely to produce meaningful lift vs testing CTA copy, placement, or surrounding context. Should recommend either reducing to 2 variants or ensuring sufficient traffic. Should still provide hypothesis framework and test setup if proceeding.
assertions: Triggers on casual phrasing
Identifies as A/B/n test (multiple variants)
Cautions about increased traffic needs for 4 variants
References sample size requirements
Questions whether button color alone is high-impact
Suggests alternative higher-impact elements to test
Provides hypothesis framework

evals.prompt: Our test has been running for 3 days and Variant B is winning with 95% confidence. Should we call it?
evals.expected_output: Should immediately address the peeking problem. Should explain that checking results early inflates false positive rates. Should recommend running for the full pre-calculated duration regardless of early results. Should explain why early significance can be misleading (regression to the mean, day-of-week effects, audience mix shifts). Should provide guidance on when it IS appropriate to stop early (sequential testing methods). Should recommend the pre-test commitment to duration.
assertions: Addresses the peeking problem directly
Explains why early significance is misleading
Recommends running for full pre-calculated duration
Mentions day-of-week effects or audience mix shifts
Explains false positive rate inflation from peeking
Mentions sequential testing as alternative approach

evals.prompt: Help me set up a multivariate test on our landing page. I want to test the headline, hero image, and CTA button simultaneously.
evals.expected_output: Should identify this as a Multivariate Test (MVT). Should explain that MVT tests combinations of elements and requires much more traffic than A/B tests. Should calculate or reference traffic needs (combinations multiply: e.g., 2 headlines × 2 images × 2 CTAs = 8 combinations). Should recommend MVT only if traffic supports it, otherwise suggest sequential A/B tests. Should build hypotheses for each element being tested. Should define interaction effects to watch for. Should provide structured test plan.
assertions: Identifies as multivariate test (MVT)
Explains MVT tests combinations of elements
Addresses dramatically higher traffic requirements
Calculates number of combinations
Suggests sequential A/B tests as alternative if traffic insufficient
Builds hypotheses for each element
Provides structured test plan

evals.prompt: What metrics should I track for an A/B test on our trial signup page? We're testing a longer form (adds company size and role fields) against the current short form.
evals.expected_output: Should apply the metrics selection framework with three tiers: primary, secondary, and guardrail metrics. Primary: form completion rate (the direct conversion metric). Secondary: lead quality metrics (SQL conversion rate, activation rate post-signup). Guardrail: overall signup volume (ensure longer form doesn't tank total signups below acceptable threshold). Should explain the tradeoff between conversion quantity and lead quality. Should note that this test needs longer observation window to measure downstream metrics.
assertions: Applies three-tier metric framework (primary, secondary, guardrail)
Identifies form completion rate as primary metric
Identifies lead quality as secondary metric
Defines guardrail metrics to protect against negative outcomes
Explains quantity vs quality tradeoff
Notes need for longer observation window for downstream metrics

evals.prompt: Can you help me write copy for our new landing page? We want to test it against the current version.
evals.expected_output: Should recognize this is primarily a copywriting task, not a test setup task. Should defer to or cross-reference the copywriting skill for writing the actual copy. May help frame the test hypothesis and setup, but should make clear that copywriting is the right skill for creating the page copy itself.
assertions: Recognizes this as primarily a copywriting task
References or defers to copywriting skill
Does not attempt to write full page copy using test setup patterns
May offer to help with test hypothesis and setup

evals.prompt: We ran an A/B test on our pricing page for 4 weeks. Control: 2.1% conversion. Variant: 2.4% conversion. 12,000 visitors per variant. Is this statistically significant? Should we ship it?
evals.expected_output: Should calculate the result under a declared analysis: 252/12,000 vs 288/12,000 gives approximately p = 0.117 for an uncorrected two-sided pooled-proportion z-test, so it does not meet alpha = 0.05. Should distinguish the 0.3 percentage-point / ~14% relative estimate from evidence for a reliably positive effect. Report uncertainty and practical business impact. Respect the pre-specified duration and stopping rule; do not recommend continuing the completed fixed-horizon test until significant. Unplanned segments are exploratory; a follow-up test needs its own plan.
assertions: Uses actual conversion counts and states the analysis assumptions
Does not call p ~0.117 significant at alpha = 0.05
Distinguishes statistical uncertainty from business value
Does not extend a completed fixed-horizon test until significant
Labels unplanned segment findings exploratory

evals.prompt: Our fixed-horizon A/B test reached its planned sample today with p = 0.04. Can I tell the CEO there is a 96% chance the change works and just a 4% chance the lift was random? We have a +2% estimate, an interval of +0.1% to +3.9%, and a higher refund rate in the variant.
evals.expected_output: Reject both probability interpretations. Explain the p-value conditional on the null model and assumptions, and repeated-sampling interval coverage without asserting a posterior probability. Consider the effect interval, practical impact and refund guardrail before recommending rollout. Do not substitute a numerical significance threshold for the business decision.
assertions: Does not interpret 1-p as the probability the variant works
Does not interpret p as the probability the result was random
Explains the conditional null-model meaning
Uses interval, business effect and refund guardrail before rollout

evals.prompt: [TST] is a home-services client (remodeler). We want to A/B test the homepage headline. Can you set it up?
evals.expected_output: Should read bml/context-rules.md and the staged file and check scope on page 00. Should pull page-level sessions and lead events from GA4 via Windsor (citing A-1/A-12) instead of asking for traffic. Should count conversions per arm per month, find that a page test can't reach sample in ~8 weeks, and step down the feasibility ladder (e.g. Google Ads experiment if A-9 shows paid volume, else before/after or don't test). Should open the plan with a 'Test verdict' line and an evidence label. Primary metric is a qualified lead (generate_lead / calls), not signups, with lead quality (I-4) as a guardrail. Should read GA4 only for the property ID in A-13, and if A-13 is OPEN, ask the user to confirm the ID first.
assertions: Reads bml/context-rules.md and checks the page 00 scope
Pulls traffic and conversions via Windsor rather than asking
Checks feasibility in conversions per arm and finds the page test too slow
Steps down the ladder to an ad-platform experiment, before/after or don't-test verdict
States a Test verdict line and an evidence label
Uses a qualified lead as primary metric with lead quality (I-4) as guardrail; no signup or SaaS metric
Uses the A-13 property ID, or asks the user to confirm it if A-13 is OPEN, before any Windsor read

evals.prompt: For [TST], a clinical client, set up a Meta A/B test with a variant that says 'Only 3 consult slots left this month — book before they're gone.' Go ahead and launch it.
evals.expected_output: Should apply context-rules.md §7 clinical rules: stop and decline the scarcity/urgency variant, naming the rule, unless a page 12 row permits it, and offer reassurance variants (process, credentials, access). Should not launch anything or use a Windsor write action; delivers a test plan plus install sheet for the account lead, launched only after the J-1 approver (A-19 if J-1 is OPEN) OKs it. Any variant claims come from rows or [NEEDS PROOF]. Should check for an APPROVED J-3 row naming the Meta Pixel (and the signer) before any lead measurement through the pixel or lead-form ads; without it, uses a platform proxy metric or stops and names the row. QA must not involve submitting patient forms.
assertions: Blocks the scarcity/urgency variant and names the clinical rule
Offers reassurance-based alternative variants
Does not launch the test or call any connector write action
Delivers a plan and install sheet for a person to launch after J-1 approval
Uses rows or [NEEDS PROOF] for any variant claim
Checks for an APPROVED J-3 row naming the Meta Pixel before measuring leads through it; without it, uses a proxy metric or stops
Does not plan test submissions on patient forms

evals.prompt: [TST] is a home-services client that's booked out through spring. Design a test to double their form leads.
evals.expected_output: Should apply the capacity gate: read B-6 and I-10, note the client is at capacity, and not design a lead-volume test. Should recommend a lead-quality or job-value test (I-4, B-7) or deferring until capacity opens, explaining why a volume 'win' would harm the client.
assertions: Reads B-6 and I-10 before designing
Does not design a lead-volume test while the client is booked out
Recommends a quality/job-value test or deferral
Explains why more leads would harm a client at capacity

evals.prompt: The Google Ads landing-page experiment for [TST] has finished. Write up the results and log the learnings.
evals.expected_output: Should read the experiment arms correctly (pointing to the ads reference on experiment arms), report effect and uncertainty under the planned analysis, and label the evidence 'Randomized (ad platform)'. Should save the results doc to the client's Drive OUTPUTS/REPORTING (resolved by ID, no Drive search or folder creation), propose a ClickUp 'research' task with the hypothesis record as its body, and turn any finding that changes something on file into a proposed context task or a §10 DRAFT row. Should not add a Learnings row to .agents/product-marketing.md. Ends with the §9 footer. Should read only the Google Ads account ID in A-13 (confirming with the user if it's OPEN) and cite figures as 'Benchmark: Windsor.ai google_ads, <account ID>, pulled <date>'.
assertions: Checks experiment arms before reading results
Labels evidence as Randomized (ad platform) and reports uncertainty
Saves to Drive OUTPUTS/REPORTING without searching Drive or creating folders
Proposes a ClickUp research task and creates nothing without approval
Routes learnings to a context task or §10 DRAFT row, never the staged file's Learnings
Ends with the context footer
Uses the A-13 account ID and cites figures with the Benchmark: Windsor.ai source label
